solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fresh chip on top of lid treated with varnish

indicators.note: letters that are treated are processed and reworked, so this pool is rearranged
the top of a word in an across clue is its first letter

explanation.surface: A fresh chip sits on a lid that has been coated in varnish, a carpenter's oddity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treated' shuffles FRESH CHIP, ON and L (the top of 'lid').
explanation.definitionFit: French polish is a shellac finish, a kind of varnish applied to fine furniture.

clue.text: Stories about university lab losing bishop's bones

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for stories goes round the other letters

parts.note: fibs are little untrue stories

indicators.note: losing says a letter is dropped from the word lab

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: Tall tales circulate about a university lab that lost a bishop's skeleton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stories' looks like the definition, but 'bones' is; 'about' wraps the fibs round the rest, and 'losing' drops the bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: The fibula is the outer lower-leg bone; this is one accepted plural form.

clue.text: Angers reserves with rule for goalies at the outset

indicators.note: putting one thing for another means substituting it
the swap is made at the first place the letter occurs, near the start of the word

parts.note: to reserve or book something is to engage it
G stands for goal, the goalkeeper's position

explanation.surface: A manager angers the reserve players by imposing a rule on goalkeepers from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' and 'at the outset' replace the first G of ENGAGES with R.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrage someone is to make them furious, a strong synonym for angering them.

clue.text: Cleaner volunteers name after fellow's turned over in fraud

indicators.note: after places one piece behind another in the answer

parts.note: a char or charwoman is a cleaner in British usage

indicators.note: turned over says the fellow's name is flipped round in this down clue

parts.note: Al is a man's name standing for any fellow
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: A cleaner and some volunteers sign a name after a man's statement is overturned in a fraud case.
explanation.walkthrough: CHAR, then LA (AL 'turned over'), then TA and N. The TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: A charlatan is an impostor or quack, a person who is a fraud.

clue.text: Demonstration of impenetrability

definitions.meaning: a demonstration that something is true
... as a noun or suffix means resistance, as in waterproof or bulletproof

explanation.surface: Showing that something cannot be broken through.
explanation.definitionFit: Proof is both evidence establishing truth and the quality of resisting penetration.

clue.text: Courageous fellow starts to cuddle unusually bony young feline

parts.note: a brave man is called a lion

indicators.note: starts to picks out the opening letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A brave man begins to cuddle a strangely skinny kitten.
explanation.definitionFit: A lion cub is the offspring of a lion, a big cat, so a juvenile feline.

clue.text: Rossetti essentially fools around with American verse form

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so the central letters are taken
around says the word for fools is turned back to front

parts.note: nits is British slang for fools, short for nitwits

explanation.surface: The poet Rossetti, at heart, plays the fool alongside an American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially' takes the two central letters of the eight-letter name; 'around' turns the fools backwards. Nits is British slang for idiots.
explanation.definitionFit: A sestina is a strict poetic form of six six-line stanzas plus an envoi, which Rossetti and others used.

clue.text: Worried, surely, facing supposedly alien craft

indicators.note: worried letters have been fretted and pulled about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone anxiously confronts what is claimed to be an extraterrestrial spaceship.
explanation.definitionFit: A flying saucer is a disc-shaped UFO, popularly believed to carry visitors from other worlds.

clue.text: Largely free to overrun island country

indicators.note: the shortened word spreads over and around the island letter
largely means most but not all of the word is kept, so its last letter goes

parts.note: liberal means free, as with generous or unrestricted

explanation.surface: An invading force largely free to overrun an island nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Largely' trims LIBERAL to LIBERA, and 'to overrun' puts it round I.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberia is a West African republic founded by freed American slaves.

clue.text: Homeless tramp is fed by street musicians

indicators.note: without home means the letter H, short for home, is removed

parts.note: a hobo is a tramp or vagrant

indicators.note: something fed by another takes it in, so the street letters go inside the word is

explanation.surface: A homeless vagrant is given food by street musicians busking nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Homeless' removes H, a standard abbreviation for home; 'fed by' makes the street go inside 'is' rather than follow it.
explanation.definitionFit: Oboists are musicians who play the oboe, a double-reed woodwind.

clue.text: Only one labourer regularly held to be working alone

parts.note: single means only one
a hand is a manual worker or labourer

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Just one workman, held to be working by himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Single-handed means done without help from anyone else, unaided.

clue.text: Bad beer not entirely withdrawn when prohibited by law

parts.note: ill means bad, as in ill effects

indicators.note: withdrawn means drawn back, so the shortened beer word is read backwards
not entirely means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: lager is a type of beer

explanation.surface: Some bad beer has been pulled from sale because it was banned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not entirely' cuts LAGER to LAGE; 'withdrawn' turns it into EGAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Illegal means forbidden by statute, the exact sense of something outlawed.

clue.text: Rebellious group in France facing lawsuit

indicators.note: facing means set in front of, so the country letter comes first

parts.note: F is the international vehicle code for France
an action is a lawsuit brought in court

explanation.surface: A band of rebels in France is confronted with legal proceedings.
explanation.definitionFit: A faction is a dissenting splinter group within a larger party or organisation.

clue.text: Breathes in sharply expressing astonishment in front of grass snakes

indicators.note: in front of here takes the front letter of grass

parts.note: asps are venomous snakes

explanation.surface: Someone inhales in shock at spotting snakes in the grass.
explanation.definitionFit: Gasps are sudden intakes of breath, typically from surprise or shock.

clue.text: Small image of lamb in hut abroad

indicators.note: abroad means widely scattered, so these letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A tiny picture of a lamb inside a hut somewhere overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: A thumbnail is a reduced-size preview picture, about as big as a thumb's nail.

clue.text: Set about getting subordinate to steal

parts.note: under means lower in rank, subordinate
to take something is to steal it

explanation.surface: A junior employee gets round to pilfering.
explanation.definitionFit: To undertake a task is to begin or embark on it, a synonym of setting about.

clue.text: Left behind in Amsterdam's west end and forbidden to implicate Rob

indicators.note: in an across clue the west end of a word is its first letter
to implicate is to fold in, so the robbery word goes inside

parts.note: banned means forbidden
to do someone is slang for robbing or cheating them

explanation.surface: Someone stranded in Amsterdam's West End, banned from involving a man called Rob.
explanation.walkthrough: 'west end' means the first letter; 'to implicate' folds the robbery inside. 'Rob' is disguised as a man's name; to 'do' someone is to swindle them.
explanation.definitionFit: Abandoned means deserted, as something left behind by its owner.

clue.text: Counsellor drives a convertible

indicators.note: convertible means capable of being changed, so these letters can be rearranged

explanation.surface: A therapist drives an open-topped car.
explanation.definitionFit: An adviser gives guidance, as a counsellor does.

clue.text: Likely to have far-reaching effect for doctor caught drinking wine

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so the wine sits inside the other letters

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
Asti is an Italian sparkling wine

explanation.surface: A doctor caught drinking wine faces serious consequences.
explanation.definitionFit: Drastic measures are radical ones, with severe and wide-ranging consequences.

clue.text: Possible partner for Austrian physicist and philosopher? About time

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the physicist's name goes round the time letter

parts.note: Ernst Mach was an Austrian physicist and philosopher

explanation.surface: Asks who might pair up with Ernst Mach and suggests the time has come.
explanation.walkthrough: A match is a suitable mate, as in a good marriage match.
explanation.definitionFit: A match is someone considered a suitable spouse or equal, so a potential partner.

clue.text: Soldier has them alternately following lawyer's instruction

indicators.note: following places one piece after another

parts.note: a man is a private soldier, as in officers and men
DA is a district attorney, an American lawyer

indicators.note: alternately picks every other letter of the word them

explanation.surface: A soldier takes instructions in turn after a lawyer's order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alternately' gives TE from 'them'; a DA is a US district attorney.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandate is an official order or authorisation, an instruction to act.

clue.text: At fault after setting up wrong produce for show

indicators.note: after places one piece behind the other in the answer
setting up in a down clue means writing the word upwards

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
out means wrong or in error, as in the figures are out

explanation.surface: Someone at fault after arranging a wrongful display.
explanation.definitionFit: To trot something out is to bring it forward for display, often tiresomely.

clue.text: Warnings about drug filled containers

parts.note: CA, short for circa, means about

indicators.note: filled says the drug letter goes inside the containers

parts.note: vats are large containers for liquids
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Health warnings about tanks laced with narcotics.
explanation.definitionFit: A caveat is a cautionary proviso, a warning to take care.

clue.text: Pinched woman's shawl

definitions.meaning: a long scarf or wrap worn over the shoulders

explanation.surface: A lady's wrap has been nicked.
explanation.definitionFit: Stole is the past tense of steal, and separately a noun for a shoulder wrap.

clue.text: Tired through overwork when ladder fell

parts.note: a ladder is a run in stockings or tights
to fell something is to bring it down

explanation.surface: A worker exhausted from too much labour when a ladder fell over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ladder' is the British word for a run in tights.
explanation.definitionFit: Run-down means exhausted and in poor health, worn out from strain.

clue.text: Rex finding it's too sloppy for a rice dish

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for Rex, Latin for king

indicators.note: sloppy means messy and disordered, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A man named Rex finds a rice dish too wet and runny.
explanation.definitionFit: Risotto is an Italian dish of rice cooked slowly in stock.

clue.text: Helping to make Kampala moderately fashionable

indicators.note: Helping to make says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something in Kampala, done in moderation, comes into vogue.
explanation.definitionFit: A la mode is French for in the current style, so modish or in vogue.

clue.text: Detect zinc say when it's present in minute amounts

parts.note: to trace something is to find or detect it
zinc is an example of a chemical element

explanation.surface: Finding zinc, for instance, when it occurs only in tiny quantities.
explanation.definitionFit: A trace element is a mineral needed or found only in very small quantities.
